# bettermemory native build

The Rust build of bettermemory 9. It reproduces the Python reference in
`src/bettermemory` exactly, so a store and its signed log written by one
open unchanged in the other. The reference behaviour is pinned by the golden
files in `tests/contract/golden`, which `tests/contract/gen_*.py` generate
from the Python code; every test here reads them from there.

Nothing here is wired into the Python product or packaged. CI builds and
tests it on Linux, macOS and Windows against fixtures made on each
("Parity on every platform").

## What the crate holds

Two crates. `crates/bettermemory-sys` holds the OS calls the standard
library does not offer safely, one function so far (`fsync`: `fsync(2)`
through `libc`, tried again on EINTR, as `os.fsync`); it is the only place
`unsafe` may appear, each use one call on a borrowed standard-library
type. The library crate, `crates/bettermemory-core` (`#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`):

Unit pyre-2, `re` as it reads a pattern: `re._parser`'s tree (`SubPattern` and its items) and `str(tree)`, the comparison of two items as Python compares them, `State` (`groups`, `opengroup`, `closegroup`, `checkgroup`, `checklookbehindgroup`), the names of `re`'s errors and of what the engine refuses, the `Tokenizer` (`match`, `get`, `getwhile`, `getuntil`, `tell`, `seek`, `error`), `_escape`, `_class_escape`, `_uniq`, the sets and flat sequences `_parse` reads (`parse_flat`), `re.escape`. Unit pyre-3a: the repeats of `_parse` with their errors (`parse::repeat`) and `SubPattern.getwidth` (`SubPattern::getwidth`). Unit pyre-3b: `re._parser.parse` (`parse::parse`) with `_parse_sub` and its rewrites, the groups, lookarounds and inline flags of `_parse`, the unpacking of plain groups, `Tokenizer.checkgroupname`, `_parse_flags` and `fix_flags`; `parse_flat` reads through it. Unit pyre-3c: the matcher's subset over the finished tree (`parse::refusal`, wired at the end of `parse`), with its nesting bound `MATCH_DEPTH`. Unit pyre-4a: `re._compiler._optimize_charset` with `_mk_bitmap` and `_bytes_to_codes` (`charset::optimize_charset`), the opcode the `IN` branch of `_compile` chooses, with the engine's refusals (`compile_class`), and `_sre`'s test of one code point against a class (`Charset::contains`). Unit pyre-4b: a parsed tree lowered to the engine's arena of nodes threaded by `next` (`lower::lower`), `_compiler._simple` (`simple`) and `_combine_flags` (`combine_flags`), the classing of each repeat as REPEAT_ONE, MIN_REPEAT_ONE or REPEAT with MAX_UNTIL or MIN_UNTIL, the lookbehind errors of `_compile`, the arena cap. Unit pyre-5a: a lowered program run as `_sre` answers `Pattern.match`, `fullmatch` and `search` with `pos` and `endpos` (`exec::exec`), with the step count, a budget and fallible growth. Unit pyre-5b: `_sre`'s ASSERT and ASSERT_NOT (`Op::Look`, `Op::LookEnd`) run in `exec` as sub-attempts on the same stack; `supports` refuses nothing. Unit pyre-6a: `re.compile` of a `str` or bytes pattern (`regex::Regex::new`, `new_bytes`), `Pattern.pattern`, `flags`, `groups`, `groupindex`, `Pattern.match`, `fullmatch`, `search`, `finditer` and `findall` with `pos` and `endpos` and `_sre`'s `must_advance` (`advance`), `re.Match` (`Match`) | `pyre.jsonl`, `pyre_unicode.jsonl`, `pyre_python.jsonl`, `pyre_lower.jsonl`, `pyre_exec.jsonl`, `pyre_api.jsonl` |

Unit pylit: `ast.literal_eval` over those tokens into a `Literal` and `claims._canonical_repr` (`literal::literal_eval`, `literal::canonical_repr`) | `pysyntax.jsonl`, `pysyntax_python.jsonl`, `pysyntax_literal.jsonl`, `pysyntax_literal_python.jsonl` |

Two tokenizer fingerprints are available: `python_tokenizer_fingerprint()`
is the reference's digest (the one the golden header pins), and
`native_tokenizer_fingerprint()` is the same input followed by
`b"\n\0\nunidata 15.1.0"`, since this build carries its own Unicode tables.

The tokenizer's word lists (stopwords, stem exceptions, acronym plurals,
the unspaced scripts) are written out by hand in `lexicon/mod.rs`. The
reference's spelling-table text, `reference_spelling_tables.json`, is a copy
of the golden `lexicon_spelling_tables.json` that the tokenizer never reads:
it is only hashed into the fingerprint. `golden_lexicon` pins that copy to
the golden file byte for byte and each hand-written list to its entry there.

Dependencies: `sha2`, `subtle` (constant-time MAC comparison), `zeroize`
(key bytes are wiped when a `Key` drops), `rusqlite` 0.43.0 with
`bundled`, `limits` and `hooks` (its bundled SQLite is 3.54.1; nothing
async) and `zlib-rs` 0.6.8 with `rust-allocator` alone (the inflate of
`gitobjects::stream`: pure Rust, no C allocator, no CPU detection at run
time, optimized in debug builds too; see "Git objects read from a
repository's files" for why this crate); the tests also use `serde_json`
to read the golden files.

## Path candidates (`verify_candidates.py`)

The candidate logic path verification stands on. The module imports
nothing from the package except `_caches` (the memo's clearer), so it is
built leaves first. It holds about 1,250 lines of Python; its port is more
than 600 lines of Rust, so it is cut into four units.

Unit 2 holds three patterns: `_BACKTICK_RE`, `_BARE_RE` and
`_DOMAIN_ROUTE_RE` as hand matchers. `_RELATIVE_CITATION_RE` moves to its
first reader (`verify.py:404`, `verify_anchoring.py:1368` and `:1696`) on

hand, so it waits for pyre-6. Unit 3 is the
candidate scan and the body parse memo, with the home directory an
argument; unit 4 the reads of the home and the disk, through the

### Unit 1, built (`verify_candidates::validate`)

Text is code points (`&[u32]`), as a Python `str` is: a body may hold a
lone surrogate, and every length, cap and index counts code points.

- `refused_spelling`: two separators first (either slash in either
  place), a NUL, or `://` anywhere.
- `escapes_root`: refused; rooted after `\` is folded to `/`; a drive
  prefix (`_DRIVE_PREFIX_RE`, `^[A-Za-z]:`, ASCII letters only, two
  comparisons); or a `..` that takes the depth below zero at any point
  of the walk.
- `fold_altsep`: `str.replace(altsep, sep)` (leftmost, not overlapping)
  when `altsep` is given and not empty.
- `is_placeholder_path`: a listed placeholder or under a listed prefix,
  as spelled or with the text after its last `.` cut, when that `.` is in
  the last segment.
- `is_single_segment_routelike`: exactly one `/` anywhere, and `s[1:]`
  non-empty and either a well-known web file name after `str.lower`
  (the crate's `unicode::lower`, so `İ` and the Kelvin sign fold as
  Python folds them) or without a dot.
- `bounded_scan_text`: at most 32,768 code points; past that, cut at the
  last space, newline or tab when it is past index 0.
- `trim_candidate`: `str.strip` (the crate's `str.isspace` table),
  `\ ` read as a space, `$HOME/` and `${HOME}/` spelled `~/`, trailing
  punctuation cut with a `)` cut only while `)` outnumbers `(`, then
  trailing slashes cut down to one code point. The reference counts both
  parentheses again for each `)` it looks at; the port counts once and
  decrements, which answers the same (no `(` is ever cut) in linear time.
- `command_shaped`: only a space or a tab makes a candidate spaced;
  `str.split` (any whitespace) cuts it into words. The first word's
  boundaries are its slashes and backslashes, one more for a drive
  (`str.isalpha` of its first code point) or a `~/` start; a later word
  without a slash is an argument when it starts with `-`, or is
  `str.isalpha` and its first code point `str.islower`. An empty split
  raises `IndexError` (`Err(IndexError)`), as the reference does.
- `anchored_candidate`: home (`~/`, longer than two code points, no
  placeholder), root (`/`, at least three, no placeholder, no single
  segment route), drive (`str.isalpha`, `:`, a separator), else None.
- `line_suffix`: `_LINE_SUFFIX_RE.match(s).group(1)`.
- `normalize_candidate`: the gates in the reference's order: over 576
  code points raw, empty or over 512 trimmed, refused, `://`, the remote
  `@` before the first colon and the first slash, the line suffix cut,
  a glob or template character, a command, the anchor.
- `is_lower`: `str.islower` of one code point: category `Ll` (the
  crate's table) or the 28 `Other_Lowercase` ranges of Unicode 15.1.0,
  written out here and pinned against every code point by the golden
  file.

**The one pattern.** `_LINE_SUFFIX_RE`,
`^(.+[\\/][^\\/:]+):\d+(?:[-:]\d+)?$`, is a hand matcher, not the
`regex` crate (whose `$` and `\d` differ). The tail after the group can
hold no separator, so whatever start the engine's backtracking tries
first, the only start that can succeed has the group end at the first `:`
after the last separator. That separator must be past index 0 with no
newline before it (`.` refuses a newline), and at least one code point
must sit between it and the colon (`[^\\/:]` accepts a newline). The tail
is `\d+` (Unicode decimal digits, the crate's `re` digit table),
optionally `-` or `:` and `\d+`, then the end or a newline that is the
last code point (`$`). The exhaustive run of the golden file (every text
of up to six code points over `a / \ : 1 - newline`) pins this reading.

No crate was added.

### Unit 2, built (`verify_candidates::patterns`)

Three hand matchers, each answering `[m.span() + m.span(1) for m in
P.finditer(text)]` over code points as a list of `Hit`. The pyre
decision (section 5, rule 3) names exactly these three as hand-written
leaves; each gains the engine's cross-check once pyre-6 lands. Their
pattern texts are already in `pyre_atom`'s inventory, which scans the
reference's source. `\w` is `unicode::is_word` (`re`'s Unicode word
class) and `\s` is `unicode::is_space`: `re`'s `\s` on a `str` pattern is
`Py_UNICODE_ISSPACE`, the set `str.isspace` reads. Neither the `regex`
crate nor pyre is used.

- `backtick_iter` (`` `([^`\n]+)` ``): not overlapping. After a match the
  search resumes after the closing backtick, so `` `a`b`c` `` yields `a`
  and `c` and never `b`; an unclosed backtick or a newline before the
  close fails that start and the search moves one code point on.
- `bare_iter` (`_BARE_RE`): `^` at position 0 only (no MULTILINE), tried
  first, else one boundary code point (`=`, `|`, `\s`, `(`, `[`, `{`, `<`,
  `"`, `'`, `,`, `;`, U+201C, U+201D, U+2018, U+2019), which the match
  consumes. The prefixes in the pattern's order: `~/`, `$HOME/`,
  `${HOME}/`, `/`, an ASCII letter, `:` and a slash or backslash. The body
  run is greedy; the continuation (`(?:(?: [A-Z][\w.\-]+)+[\\/][body]+)*`)
  takes its greedy spaced words, needs a separator after the last, then a
  body run, and otherwise gives back to the last complete continuation.
- `domain_route_iter` (`_DOMAIN_ROUTE_RE`): `domain_at` of the pyre
  design's `hw/parts_model_det.py`: the two lookbehinds, an optional `.`,
  a `[\w-]` label, one or more `.label`, `/`, and `[\w.\-]+` as group 1.

**Why one path per start equals `re`.** The doc comment of `patterns.rs`
gives the argument per pattern: each class next to a give-back point is
disjoint from the code point that must follow, so a shorter run never lets
the rest of the pattern match where the greedy run failed. The template,
`hw/parts_model_det.py`, was checked against `re` on 2,146,278 texts; the
golden sweeps check the port on 772,470 more.

**Linear.** A failed backtick start scanned a run holding no backtick. A
bare start needs a boundary, which no body or spaced word holds, and a
continuation scan is either consumed by the match or stops at a space
before a word that cannot open a prefix. A domain start inside a `[\w-]`
run or at a later label of a dotted run is refused by a lookbehind in
constant time, so a token is scanned from at most two starts.
`verify_candidates_patterns_robustness` pins 200,000 code points of each
hostile shape within `TENFOLD` of a tenth of it.

The first lookbehind of `_DOMAIN_ROUTE_RE` (`(?<![\w-])`) changes no
`finditer` answer: a start inside a label run fails exactly as the run's
own start does, and a match ends before a code point outside `[\w-]`. It
only saves work, as its comment says; the port keeps it for the same
reason.

The caller (unit 3) passes the masked text, not the raw body, to the bare
scan, so these matchers and their fixtures do not model the masking
(decision rule 7: the caller's domain is declared here).

No crate was added.

### Unit 3, built (`verify_candidates::scan`)

`_normalize_for_compare` (326-343), `_scan_candidates` (562-677) and
`_extract_candidates` (549-559) without its body parse memo. The home
directory is an argument: `home` is what `~` expands to (`$HOME`, else
the running user's password entry; None when neither is known) and
`lookup` answers `pwd.getpwnam(name)` for `~name` as a `UserHome`: the
`pw_dir`, `Unknown` for an unknown name, or `Refused` for a name
`getpwnam` rejects with `ValueError`. Unit 4 reads both from the machine.

- `normalize_for_compare`: `str(Path(raw).expanduser())` under
  `PosixPath`. The text is parsed as `_parse_path` parses it (exactly two
  leading slashes keep a `//` root, one or three or more give `/`; empty
  and `.` parts are dropped, `..` stays). When there is no root and the
  first part starts with `~`, `posixpath.expanduser` of that part gives
  the home with trailing slashes cut, or `/` when nothing is left; a home
  that is unknown, or that itself starts with `~`, is
  `Err(CompareError::Home)`: the reference catches only `OSError` and
  `ValueError`, so the `RuntimeError` escapes. A `~user` name that
  `pwd.getpwnam` refuses with `ValueError` (a NUL, or a surrogate the
  filesystem encoding cannot encode; `getpwnam_refuses` states the rule
  and the lookup answers `UserHome::Refused`) gives the raw text back,
  since the reference's handler catches that `ValueError`. The expanded home is parsed again and the rest
  of the parts appended.
- `scan_candidates`: the body bounded (`bounded_scan_text`); the set of
  `_DOMAIN_ROUTE_RE` group 1 over that body; the backtick pass, each
  group `str.strip`ped, normalized, kept unless a route, deduplicated on
  `normalize_for_compare`, the cap checked after each append and
  returning at once; every backtick span (delimiters included) masked
  with spaces of the same length, kept or not; then the bare pass over
  the masked text, its ambiguity flag set when the candidate needed no
  trim and the two code points after the group are a U+0020 and a code
  point `str.islower` refuses. A key seen before only downgrades a stored
  ambiguity; `bare_spaced` is a U+0020 in the candidate. The cap breaks
  after an append. `_normalize_candidate`'s `IndexError` and
  `expanduser`'s `RuntimeError` both escape (`ScanError`), at the same
  candidate as in the reference, since both passes take their matches in
  order.
- `extract_candidates(body, home, lookup)`: `[]` for an empty body,
  else the scan. The memo, a later unit, wraps it unchanged. It takes no
  `attested` argument, as the reference's `_extract_candidates` takes
  none.

**Patterns.** The scan calls the three hand matchers of unit 2 and adds
no pattern; nothing goes into the engine's inventory.

**Windows.** Only the POSIX flavour of `Path` is ported. Under
`WindowsPath` the reference parses drives, UNC roots and both
separators; that flavour is not built here. On a target that is not
Unix, `normalize_for_compare` of a non-empty text answers
`CompareError::NotPorted` and the scan of a non-empty body
`ScanError::NotPorted`. The fixtures that pin the comparison form and
the kills test are POSIX only (`verify_candidates_scan_not_posix`
records the gap, class os, and checks the decline).

### What the reference does that looks wrong (not changed)

- A candidate that trims to whitespace alone raises. `\ \ .` in
  backticks strips to itself, reads as two spaces and a period, loses the
  period, and `_command_shaped` takes `parts[0]` of an empty split:
  `IndexError` out of `_normalize_candidate`, and so out of
  `_scan_candidates` for any body holding `` `\ \ .` ``. Reproduce:
  `verify_candidates._normalize_candidate("\\ \\ .")`. The port answers
  `Err(IndexError)`.
- `$` admits a final newline: `_normalize_candidate("/a/foo.py:1\n.")`
  is `/a/foo.py` (the period trimmed, the newline left, the suffix cut).
- `_MAX_BODY_SCAN_BYTES` counts code points, not bytes, and the cut
  looks only for a space, a newline or a tab: a body whose only
  whitespace past index 0 is `\r` or U+00A0 keeps the hard cut its
  docstring says never happens mid-token. Whitespace at index 0 alone
  also keeps the hard cut.
- `_normalize_candidate`'s own `"://" in s` test can never refuse
  anything: `_refused_spelling` refused it one line before.
- `_is_single_segment_routelike` reads `s[1:]` whatever `s[0]` is:
  `a/b` is routelike. Its only caller passes texts that start with `/`.
- Only a space or a tab marks a spaced candidate, so a no-break space
  inside an argument-shaped path (`/a/b x c/d`) splits it as
  whitespace yet the candidate is refused as a command, while
  `/a/b x/c` alone is kept with the no-break space in it.

`gen_verify_candidates.py` writes two files. A case whose texts are all
ASCII goes in `verify_candidates.jsonl` (every table answers ASCII the
same in every Unicode release); one with a code point past ASCII, and the
ranges `str.islower` holds over every code point, go in
`verify_candidates_unicode.jsonl`, gated on the Unicode data. No case
depends on the Python release or the platform. Exhaustive runs record
only the texts whose answer is not the default, and the test enumerates
the same texts in `itertools.product`'s order, so a missing hit fails.

Unit 2's rows hold no path, error text or repr, and `re` answers the
three patterns alike under Python 3.11 to 3.14 and on every platform, so
`verify_candidates_patterns.jsonl` is ungated and every CI job checks it.
A text or fragment past Latin-1 other than the four typographic quotes
goes in `verify_candidates_patterns_unicode.jsonl`, gated on the Unicode
data only. Each file holds chosen texts with their matches and, per
pattern, digest rows: every text joined from zero to `depth` fragments in
`itertools.product`'s order, the count and the SHA-256 of the answers.

Unit 3's files are POSIX only (`POSIX_ONLY` in `generate.py`): the
reference spells the comparison form through the host's `Path`. The
home is recorded, never read: the generator sets `$HOME` to the row's
home (or removes it, with the password entry of the running user
unknown) and replaces `pwd` with a table in the header. Rows pin each
`Path` collapse (slash runs, `//`, trailing slash, `.` parts), each home
spelling, the unknown home as the error row, each pass, the masking, the
ambiguity tail and its downgrade, the routes, the cap in each pass and
past the scan bound, and two digest sweeps of 7,381 and 9,331 bodies.
A body past ASCII goes in `verify_candidates_scan_unicode.jsonl`, gated
on the Unicode data as well.

## Body candidates of path drift (`path_drift_steps.py`)

`_check_body_candidates` (29-169), the one function of the module,
built whole in `path_drift_steps.rs` (about 90 lines). It needs nothing
built: `_path_exists` and `_is_multi_segment_routelike` (unit 4 of
`verify_candidates`) and the claim key function reach it as closures
(`exists`, `routelike`, `keys`), and the buckets with the seen set are a
`Buckets` struct handed in by `&mut`.

- The closures are called in the reference's order: `exists(path)` then
  `keys(path)`; in the spaced arm `keys(prefix)` then `exists(prefix)`,
  the seen test only when the prefix exists (the `and` short-circuit);
  `routelike(path)` only after the spaced and ambiguous arms decline.
- The prefix is `path.split(" ", 1)[0]`: U+0020 only.
- `dropped_as_route` is appended unguarded, as the reference does; a
  caller that hands one route twice gets it twice.
- Paths are `String`: a candidate holding a lone surrogate cannot reach
  this port. The caller that joins the scan to this pass decides how such
  a candidate travels.

| test | golden file | class |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `golden_path_drift_steps`: `path_drift_steps_every_case` | `path_drift_steps.jsonl` | i |
| `path_drift_steps_kills` (7) | none | i |

`gen_path_drift_steps.py` replaces both module-level checks with recorded
sets and logs every closure call. Its rows are every combination of the
flags, existence, attestation, route reading, prefix existence and a
seen key handed in (with the path existing, route and prefix are never
read), plus multi-candidate rows for shared keys, a prefix met twice, a
tab before the space and duplicate routes. It holds no path of the host
and is ungated.

## Path attestations (`attestation_paths.py`)

`attestation_paths.rs` is the whole Python module (290 lines of
reference), built in one unit.
No regular expression is in it.

| function | reference lines | what it needs of the machine | status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `LiteralPaths`, `ReferencePaths` (`Paths`, `Kind`), `path_mode` | 29-44 | nothing | built |
| `interpret_path` | 45-72 | `os.name`, `os.lstat`, `os.path.expanduser` (through `target_path`) | built |
| `_may_be_literal` | 73-87 | `os.lstat` | built |
| `joined_path` | 88-100 | as `interpret_path` | built |
| `_REFERENCE_ROOT`, `absolute_spelling`, `literal_path`, `reference_path` | 101-146 | nothing (`str.isalpha` and `str.strip` from the crate's Unicode tables) | built |
| `placeholder_spelling` | 147-172 | as `interpret_path` | built |
| `target_path` | 173-200 | `os.path.expanduser`, the host's `os.path.normpath`; `ntpath.normcase` on a Windows host | built |
| `record_paths`, `commit_paths` | 201-233 | nothing | built |
| `compile_targets` | 234-278 | as `interpret_path` | built |
| `unverifiable_inputs` | 279-290 | the probe, a closure | built |

**The host is a trait** (`Host`): `nt()` is `os.name == "nt"` and picks
the flavour of `os.path` (`normpath` after `expanduser`); `expanduser`
answers text or what it raised; `lstat` answers whether `os.lstat`
raised and what. `FsHost` asks a `fsdata::Fs` (`lstat_result`), the path
encoded as `os.fsencode` does on POSIX (a code point it refuses is the
ValueError `os.lstat` raises); under `nt` a lone surrogate is not ported.
`nt_normcase` is `ntpath.normcase`: Python's own (`/` to `\`, then
`str.lower`) off Windows, and on a Windows host `LCMapStringEx`, which is
not ported, so by default it declines there (`Raised::NotPorted`, caught
by no clause). With `fsdata`'s Windows flavour this is the crate's stated
Windows gap (ENG-124); `attestation_paths_not_posix` records it.

**Raises.** `Raised` holds what a call raises: `Index` (the IndexError
`_normalize_candidate` raises, caught by none of the module's clauses),
`Value`, `Os` (each caught by `except (OSError, ValueError,
RuntimeError)`), `Other` (any other class the host raises, such as the
KeyError of an `expanduser`; not caught) and `NotPorted`.

**What is written here.** `nt_splitdrive` (`ntpath.splitdrive`, over the
crate's `splitroot`, now `pub(crate)`) and `commonpath` for both flavours,
None where the reference raises ValueError (absolute beside relative,
rooted beside not, two drives). `ntpath.commonpath` compares lowered
parts and returns the first path's own spelling, as 3.13 does.

**Decisions.** The record helpers take a `Record` with the four fields
they read, the two maps ordered (`Targets`), since no record model of
`models.py` exists yet. `compile_targets` keeps a dict's order: a repeated
input keeps its first place and its last value, through an index of the
keys so that many inputs cost what a dict costs; the legacy list may
repeat. `Mode::parse` is the ValueError `compile_targets` raises for a
mode it does not know; the other functions take a `Mode`. An empty root
holds nothing: `commonpath((".", "x"))` is the empty text, which is not
`.`, so every relative target under `root=""` raises; the port
reproduces it.

**Fixtures.** `gen_attestation_paths` replaces the module's `os` with a
scripted one (`name`, a `path` with the module's `normpath` and a scripted
`expanduser`, a scripted `lstat` by the path's last character), so
`attestation_paths.jsonl` is the same on every host and not gated: named
spellings under both hosts with every function, long and surrogate
spellings by digest, the record helpers, `compile_targets` over lists,
roots and modes, and a seeded sweep (1,200 spellings of 1 to 6 pieces
under both hosts, every function, eight roots, three modes, by count and
SHA-256). `attestation_paths_posix.jsonl` (POSIX only) runs the real `os`
over a scratch tree with a file, a folder, a dangling link, a link loop
and a mode-000 folder; `golden_attestation_paths_posix` runs `FsHost` over
`StdFs` there.

`project_file.rs` is unit 1. The module's map:

| `Walk` | 140-233 | nothing | built (unit 3, `project_walk.rs`) |

| `above_start`, `find` | 263-314 | the walk | built (unit 3) |
| `write` | 317-361 | the file system's writes (`WriteEffects`), random bytes | built (unit 3) |
| `render` | 364-378 | nothing | built (unit 1) |
| `_absolute` | 384-385 | `os.path.abspath` (`hostpath::text::abspath`) | unit 2 |
| `_walk`, `_look` | 388-410 | `os.stat` (`Fs::stat`), `path_missing`, `Fs::strerror` | built (unit 3) |
| `_evicted`, `_parse_stat` | 413-437 | `sys.platform == "darwin"` (an argument), `StatResult.flags` and `file_attributes` | unit 2 |
| `_read_bounded` | 440-460 | `fsdata`'s non-blocking `open_result`, `fstat_result`, `read_once`, `close` | unit 2 |

| `_bad_name`, `_bad_char`, `_toml_string` | 502-523 | nothing | built (unit 1) |

**The cut.** The lane's plan built `parse` with unit 1 unless the two
modules of the lane passed 600 lines of Rust source; `attestation_paths`
alone is 560, so `parse` and the reads under it are unit 2
(`project_file-2`: `parse`, `_absolute`, `_evicted`, `_parse_stat`,
`_read_bounded`, `_from_table`, `_os_text`, with their fixtures: every
error reason over scratch files, sizes 65,535 to 65,537, bytes that are
not UTF-8, `tomllib`'s messages in a Python-gated sibling, and a FIFO,
links and modes with `strerror` texts in a POSIX-only file gated on the
platform). The walk, `find` and `write` are unit 3.
`capture::location`'s `ProjectFileRef` and the membership records stay as
they are.

**As built.** `ProjectFile` and `ProjectFileError` hold their path as the
text of the reference's `Path`; `directory` is `dirname` of it, and `.`
where that is empty, as `Path.parent` gives for one relative component. `line`
quotes the path (`printable::quoted`). `mint_id` takes the random bytes
`secrets.randbits` reads (17) and writes them through
`checkout_token::random_crockford`. `render` answers None where
`.encode("utf-8")` raises (a lone surrogate in the id or the name).
`_toml_string` escapes `"` and `\` with a backslash and every C0
character and DEL as `\u` and four capital hex digits; nothing past
DEL is escaped (U+0085 and U+2028 pass), which `_bad_name` refuses in a
name read back.

**`_ID_RE`.** The pattern `bmp_[<CROCKFORD>]{26}` under `fullmatch` has no
choice; it is matched by hand (`id_text`: the prefix, then
`checkout_token::token_text`), under rule 3 of the regular expression
decision as the lane names it, with the engine's cross-check (pyre-8)
once pyre-6 is in the crate. It is built by an f-string, so the pyre
inventory's scan of literal patterns does not hold it; pyre-7 builds it
from the module's own text.

**Fixtures.** `project_file.jsonl` (not gated): the error's line over
paths with quotes, line breaks and an escape sequence, `render` with every
C0 character, DEL and past ASCII and with a lone surrogate, `mint_id` over
three byte strings, `_ID_RE.fullmatch` over ids one step from valid, and
every code point `_bad_char` refuses.

### Unit 3: the walk and `write` (`project_walk.rs`)

`project_walk.rs` holds unit 3 apart from `project_file.rs`, so that it
builds beside unit 2, which edits that file. It reads `ProjectFile`,
`ProjectFileError`, `Found`, `Above`, `render`, `mint_id`, `bad_name` and
`directory` from unit 1.

- `Walk` keeps its flavour beside the reference's fields. `items`,
  `files`, `errors`, `root`, `nested`, `folder`, `enclosing`, `nearest`,
  `boundaries` and `placement` answer as the properties do; `placement`
  of a file not on the walk is the ValueError `<path> is not on this
  walk`.
- Paths are kept as `Path` text (`pure_text`): under Windows a
  drive-only UNC path (`\\srv\sh`, `\\?\UNC\srv\sh`) gains the root
  separator `PureWindowsPath` writes and `ntpath.abspath` leaves off, so
  a repository at a bare share keeps its file as the root.
- Two paths are equal as `PurePath.__eq__` compares them (`path_eq`): the
  text under POSIX, `str.lower` of it under Windows. A `ProjectFile` is
  equal to another by its four fields with that path equality, as the
  dataclass compares them.
- `Path.parent` is unit 1's `directory`; `Path.is_relative_to` (3.13) is
  lexical: equal, or equal to one of the parents (`is_relative_to`), so
  `/r/ab` is not under `/r/a`. `directory / NAME` is `os.path.join`.
- `above_start` and `find` follow the reference's order: the cwd made
  absolute, the start, the check of a cached `above` (its message spells
  a missing start `None`), the root made absolute, the inner walk (from
  the root where the cwd is not under it), then the walk above unless a
  cached `above` is given, which is used as it is and never read again.
- `_walk` stops after the stop folder or the filesystem root.
- `_look` stats with links followed (`Fs::stat`), as `os.stat` does; the
  lane's plan named `lstat_result`, which would read a linked
  `bettermemory.toml` as a link and differ from the reference. A missing
  path (`probe::path_missing`) is no item; a ValueError of the stat (a
  NUL) is raised, since `except OSError` does not catch it; any other
  error is an `unreadable` item whose detail is `Fs::strerror`, and where
  the file system has no text the port declines (`Fault::NotPorted`;
  `str(exc)` is not reproduced). A path is encoded with `fsencode`
  (UTF-8, `surrogateescape`); a lone surrogate it cannot carry is
  `Fault::Encode`.
- The parse is the caller's closure `look_file(path, &StatResult)`,
  standing for unit 2's `_parse_stat`.
- `_absolute` is `hostpath::text::abspath` over a `Process`; where
  `os.getcwd()` raises, `Fault::Cwd`. Under the Windows flavour on a
  Windows host `abspath` asks `nt._getfullpathname`, which the crate does
  not port (ENG-124): the caller's `Process` answers it.
- `write` checks the name, makes the folder absolute, asks `is_dir`,
  mints the id from the given random bytes (a count other than 17 is
  `Fault::NotPorted`), renders (a lone surrogate in the name is
  `Fault::Encode`, before anything is written), then either
  `atomic_write_bytes(path, body, mode=0o644)` (rebind) or the exclusive
  create with mode 0o644, the write loop, `fsync_file` and the close. An
  error of the create is raised with nothing removed. An error of a write
  or of the close removes the file quietly and is raised; where both
  fail, the close's error is raised, as an exception in a `finally`
  replaces the one in flight. `fsync_dir` follows a written file. Its
  effects are the trait `WriteEffects`; no implementation over the disk
  is in the crate yet (the golden test holds one over `std::fs`).
- The write loop slices by the count `os.write` answers and stops only
  when nothing is left, as the reference's does: a write that answers 0
  for a non-empty buffer loops for ever in both.

**Fixtures.** `project_walk.jsonl` (POSIX only: links, a mode-000 folder,
strerror texts, paths spelled by the host's `Path`): a `tree` row, then
24 `find` rows over it (files at the cwd, between, at the root and above
it, a boundary file, malformed files, a `bettermemory.toml` that is a
folder, a linked, a dangling and a looping link, a cwd below a regular
file, a mode-000 folder, a root not above the cwd, no repository, the
root `/`, a cached `above` reused after a file above changed, and three
mismatched caches), each with the reference's parse of every file it
can stat (`pf`), and 12 `write` rows (written, `FileExistsError`,
rebind, `ValueError` for control characters and separators,
`FileNotFoundError` for a missing folder and a file, the
`UnicodeEncodeError` of a lone surrogate, a folder spelled with `..`),
each with the SHA-256 of the file after the call. Every path is spelled
relative to the scratch folder. `golden_project_walk.rs` builds the same
tree and walks it with `pf` as the parse; `project_walk_not_posix.rs`
records the gap on Windows (class os). `project_walk_kills.rs` and
`project_walk_robustness.rs` run over `MemFs` and scripted writes on
every host; the kills cover a repository at a bare UNC share under the
Windows flavour and the decline on an empty strerror text, and the
robustness test walks 2,000 levels within the 1.2 s the reference took.

## Verification staleness and phrase-match attribution

`src/bettermemory/verify_status.py` (247 lines) and
`src/bettermemory/attribution.py` (342 lines), read at 465bc600, are two
leaves: neither imports the package. Both are built whole, in one unit
(`verify_status.rs` and `attribution.rs`, 525 lines of source).

### The map

| function | reference lines | needs from the machine | status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `VerificationStatus.to_dict` | verify_status 88-111 | nothing | built |
| `_stale_recommendation`, `_remote_recommendation`, `_NEVER_RECOMMENDATION` | verify_status 115-142 | nothing | built |
| `remote_verification_status` | verify_status 146-169 | nothing | built |
| `compute_verification_status` | verify_status 172-240 | the clock, as the argument `now` | built |
| `_candidate_sentences`, `_SENTENCE_SPLIT_RE` (190), `_PUNCT_STRIP_RE` (194), `_TOKEN_RE` (173) | attribution 197-234 | Unicode data (`\s`, `\w`, `str.lower`) | built |
| `_normalize` | attribution 237-252 | Unicode data (NFC, `str.lower`, `\s`) | built |
| `_content_token_set` | attribution 255-273 | Unicode data (through `_normalize`) | built |
| `attribute_uses` | attribution 276-308 | nothing more | built |
| `_sentence_matches` | attribution 311-342 | nothing more | built |

### verify_status

- `compute_verification_status(last_verified_at, now, stale_after_days)`
  answers `Ok(VerificationStatus)` or `Err(NaiveAwareMix)`, the
  reference's TypeError when a naive `now` meets a stamp (a naive stamp is
  made UTC first; a missing stamp asks nothing of the clock, so a naive
  `now` then answers `never`). The clock is an argument, as in the
  reference.
- The elapsed time is the exact microsecond difference of the two
  instants divided by 10^6 and rounded once to nearest even
  (`micros_to_seconds`, `timedelta.total_seconds` as CPython's `int /
  int`). Past 2^53 microseconds (about 285 years) a float conversion
  before the division would round twice; the long
  division keeps one rounding. `age_days` is CPython's float floor
  division (`float_floor_div`, `_float_div_mod` line for line) of the
  rounded seconds, so 3,000,000 days less a microsecond counts 3,000,000
  days, as the reference does, where integer arithmetic counts one fewer.
- The stale test is the reference's float-against-int comparison, exact
  (`float_gt_int`): elapsed seconds strictly greater than the threshold's
  seconds. A threshold below zero is clamped to zero.
- `stale_after_days` is an `i64`. The reference takes any `int` (a
  `bool` too, which `max(0, True)` keeps as `True` and `to_dict` writes
  as `true`); every caller passes the constant 30, so values outside
  64 bits and booleans are outside the port's domain.
- `to_dict` is a `PyValue` dict in the reference's key order, the stamp
  spelled by `DateTime::isoformat_utc` (`isoformat()` with each `+00:00`
  made `Z`).

### attribution

Texts are code points, so a lone surrogate passes as in the reference.
`attribute_uses` takes the memories as `(id, body)` pairs in the dict's
order. The three patterns are hand-written matchers; no regex crate is
used and none is added:

- `_SENTENCE_SPLIT_RE`, `(?:[.!?]\s+|\n+)` with `re.split`: a scan that
  tries the first alternative at each position, then the second, each run
  greedy; no capture group, so only the pieces are kept. `\s` is
  `str.isspace` (`Py_UNICODE_ISSPACE`, which `re`'s Unicode `\s`,
  `str.split()` and `str.strip()` all read; it includes U+001C to U+001F
  and U+0085), so the semantics are equal for every input.
- `_PUNCT_STRIP_RE`, `^[^\w]+|[^\w]+$` with `sub("")`, applied to tokens
  `str.split()` made: the leading run of non-word code points, then the
  trailing run of what is left. `$` also matches before a final newline,
  and no such token holds one. `\w` is `unicode::is_word`, `re`'s table.
- `_TOKEN_RE`, `[a-z0-9_]+` with `findall`: maximal ASCII runs.

`needle in haystack` is a Knuth-Morris-Pratt search over code points,
linear, so a needle built to make a naive search quadratic costs what it
costs the reference (whose search is CPython's two-way and Horspool mix).
The ratios are `int / int` of counts below 2^53, so IEEE division of the
two counts is the reference's quotient. `_STOPWORDS` is written out sorted
and pinned to the reference's set by the golden header.

### Reference findings (reproduced)

1. An offset with seconds keeps them after `Z`: a stamp at `+00:00:30`
   spells `2026-01-01T00:00:00Z:30` in `to_dict` and in the remote
   recommendation (`str.replace` replaces the prefix of the offset).
   Reproduction: `remote_verification_status(datetime(2026, 1, 1,
   tzinfo=timezone(timedelta(seconds=30)))).to_dict()["last_verified_at"]`.
2. `to_dict`'s docstring says the stamp is normalised to `Z`; an aware
   stamp at another offset is kept at that offset (`+02:00`), never
   converted to UTC. Reproduction: `compute_verification_status(
   datetime(2026, 1, 1, tzinfo=timezone(timedelta(hours=2))),
   now=datetime(2026, 3, 1, tzinfo=timezone.utc)).to_dict()`.
3. The verbatim tier compares the excerpt, which is cut to 500 code
   points before matching, so a reply holding only the first 500 code
   points of a longer sentence is attributed that sentence. Reproduction:
   `b = "start " + "alpha " * 120 + " end"; attribute_uses({"m": b},
   b[:500])` answers a match.
4. `_content_token_set` keeps only ASCII `[a-z0-9_]`, so after NFC a
   precomposed letter drops out of a token (`café` gives `caf`), and a
   sentence of words outside ASCII has no content tokens and can match
   only verbatim. The docstring describes this; it is recorded because
   the containment tier is silent for such text.

### Fixtures and tests

- `tests/contract/gen_verify_status.py` writes `verify_status.jsonl`
  (not gated, 436 cases, about 100 KB): never verified over thirteen
  thresholds; thirteen distances around the 30-day bound in microseconds
  over six thresholds; eleven offsets on the stamp against eleven on the
  clock (naive among them, the TypeError included); remote stamps; the
  ends of the calendar, where the microsecond count passes 2^53; and 120
  seeded pairs. Recommendations are written by reference to the header's
  texts, which pin each recommendation function.
- `tests/contract/gen_attribution.py` writes `attribution.jsonl` (cases
  whose inputs are ASCII, not gated) and `attribution_unicode.jsonl`
  (every other case, gated on the Unicode version): each of the four
  inner functions on its own and `attribute_uses` whole, over hand-picked
  bodies for every bound (30 characters before and after the terminal
  strip, 6 tokens, the 0.80 stopword ratio, the 0.60 containment ratio,
  the 4-token floor, the 500-character cut) and seeded random bodies.
- Rust: `golden_verify_status.rs`, `golden_attribution.rs` (both files),
  `verify_status_kills.rs`, `attribution_kills.rs` and
  `attribution_robustness.rs` (2,000,000-character replies, 7,800,000-
  character bodies, 20,000 sentences, 10,000 memories, the calendar's
  ends with offsets of a day less a microsecond, `i64::MIN` and
  `i64::MAX` thresholds; each bounded at three times the reference's
  time, twenty times that in a debug build).

Nothing of either module is left for a later unit. The callers
(`verify.py`'s re-export, `_response.ResponseBuilder.apply_trust`, the
Stop hook) are not ported here.

## ResponseBuilder's search and list serializers (`_response.py`)

`src/bettermemory/_response.py`, read at 7be0e20e, holds `ResponseBuilder`.
This unit (`response_rows.rs`, 189 lines of source) ports the three
methods that turn a search hit, a list row and a tombstone row into the
dict the tools return, and the constant `SIMILAR_HITS_SHOWN`. The
remaining methods (the attach passes and the write responses; `render_hit`
is in `response_render`)
are a later unit that adds a second `impl ResponseBuilder` block in its
own file.

| Function | Reference lines | Needs from the machine | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SIMILAR_HITS_SHOWN` | 113 | nothing | built |
| `ResponseBuilder.__init__` | 746-749 | nothing | built (`ResponseBuilder::new`, the field `stale_after_days`) |
| `hit_to_dict` | 751-886 | the clock, as the argument `now` | built |
| `summary_to_dict` | 1025-1079 | the clock, as the argument `now` | built |
| `tombstone_summary_to_dict` | 1081-1104 | nothing | built |

Each method answers a `PyValue::Dict` whose keys are in the reference's
insertion order, so `json::dumps` with the defaults writes the
reference's text byte for byte; the golden file compares that text.

- `hit_to_dict` takes the verdict from `compute_staleness_verdict` with
  the claim-anchored count as the missing count, the full missing list's
  length as `cited_missing` and no commit leg, as the reference does. The
  `path_drift` block opens on the missing, verified, expected-absent and
  present-but-attested-absent buckets only; the route and claim-anchored
  buckets ride in it but never open it. So a hit whose only bucket is the
  claim-anchored one carries a raised verdict and no block, which the
  golden file pins (the reference never builds such a hit, since the
  anchored set is a subset of the missing one).
- The counts `path_drift_checked` and `path_drift_missing` ship as
  given; nothing checks them against the lists.
- A naive `now` against an aware stamp is the reference's `TypeError`
  from `compute_verification_status`; the two clocked methods answer it
  as `Err(NaiveAwareMix)`. A naive stamp is rendered without an offset,
  and every `+00:00` in a stamp becomes `Z` (`DateTime::isoformat_utc`).
- `summary_to_dict` adds `actor` with the declared `client` and `model`
  that are not None, in that order, and omits it when neither is set; an
  empty string counts as declared.
- No regular expression is involved.

Fixtures: `tests/contract/gen_response_hits.py` builds the three models
with `model_construct` and writes `response_hits.jsonl` (not gated, 46
cases): every gate of the `path_drift` block and its additive keys, the
verdict tiers, the threshold edges, offsets and naive stamps, the
`TypeError`, the floats `json` spells its own way (NaN, the infinities,
negative zero) and texts with a lone surrogate (through `text_field`).
Tests: `golden_response_hits`, `response_hits_kills` and
`response_hits_robustness` (integer and calendar bounds, 200,000 paths
per bucket, linear growth).

hook, and their stdin. Its whole is well past 600 lines of Rust, so it is
cut into units, leaves first; each lands in its own flat file beside

`hook_cli.rs`) so that no two units edit one file.

### The map

| function | reference lines | needs from the machine | status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `_ATTRIBUTION_LOOKBACK_SECONDS` (alias of `audit.ATTRIBUTION_LOOKBACK_SECONDS`, audit 185) | 189 | nothing | hook-1a |
| `_STDIN_PAYLOAD_CAP_BYTES` | 207 | nothing | hook-1a |
| `_read_payload` | 210-221 | nothing | hook-1a |
| `_payload_text` | 224-227 | nothing | hook-1a |
| `_emit_hook_attributions` | 1066-1170 | the store, the recorder, the session join, the clock | hook-1a, all four as arguments |
| `_pending_retrievals` | 1173-1248 | the clock (`utcnow`) | hook-1a, the clock as an argument |
| `_utcnow`, `is_synthetic_prompt`, `human_prompt`, `_origin_for` | 174-256 | the clock, the origin | later |
| `audit_transcript`, `run_audit`, `_audit_turn` | 258-587 | the transcript, the store, the recorder | later |
| `_stop_window` to `_settle_stop_interrupted` | 588-948 | the store, the recorder, the probe | later |
| `run_prompt_recall`, `prompt_main`, `main` | 949-1065, 1251-1352 | stdin, the store, the configuration | later |

### Unit hook-1a (`hook.rs`)

- `ATTRIBUTION_LOOKBACK_SECONDS` (600) is defined in `hook.rs`; its home
  is `audit.py`, and it moves to the port of that module when one exists.
  `STDIN_PAYLOAD_CAP_BYTES` is 64 KiB; the bounded read itself is the
  caller's.
- `read_payload(text)` strips as `str.strip` does (`unicode::py_strip`,
  `str.isspace` over the Unicode tables; the helper that
  `capture::remote` held privately is now this one public function) and
  reads the rest with `json::loads_detailed`. A blank text, a decode
  failure and a value that is not a dict answer an empty dict. The
  reference catches only `JSONDecodeError`, so an integer past 4300
  digits is `Err(LoadError::IntDigits)` (its ValueError) and a payload
  nested past the decoder's budget is `Err(LoadError::Recursion)` (its
  RecursionError). The depth at which the reference's RecursionError
  starts follows the interpreter's recursion limit and stack; the
  crate's budget is CPython 3.13.13's, and the exact Python depth is not
  matched bit for bit.
- `payload_text(payload, name)`: the field when it is a non-empty `str`.
- `pending_retrievals(events, now, retrieval_session_id,
  used_session_ids, lookback_seconds)`: `now` is the clock the
  reference reads through `utcnow()`. The window test is the reference's
  float comparison, `ts.timestamp() < now.timestamp() - lookback`, each
  timestamp the microsecond count since the epoch divided once
  (`verify_status::micros_to_seconds`): in year 9000 an event a
  microsecond older than the cutoff rounds onto it and is kept, where a
  comparison of microseconds drops it. Every `or` reads Python
  truthiness (`events::truthy`), kinds and sessions match only a `str`
  equal to the one named, and ids are kept only from a `list` of `str`.
  An event that is not a dict is `Err(ScanError::NotADict)` (the
  reference's AttributeError on `event.get`); a `use` row in the window
  whose session is unhashable (a list, a dict, a tuple holding one) is
  `Err(ScanError::Unhashable)` (its TypeError from `in` on a set), while
  a retrieval row with such a session is skipped by `!=` as in the
  reference. The answer is a `BTreeSet`, whose order is the code-point
  order of `sorted`.
- `emit_hook_attributions(turn, load_one, recorder, latest_session)`:
  `load_one` answers a body, None where the store raises
  `MemoryNotFoundError` or `TombstonedError`, or the store's error; the
  recorder is the trait `RowSink` (`record(kind, fields)`, the fields in
  the keyword order the reference passes); `latest_session` is
  `sessions._latest_in_process_session`, asked only when
  `server_session` is None. Bodies are loaded in code-point order, the
  attributed `use` row (ids, outcome, auto, attribution,
  claim_excerpts, triggered_from, then client_model when given, an
  empty one included) comes before the auto row of the unmatched ids,
  and an error of the store or the recorder ends the call where the
  reference's exception would.
- No regular expression is matched here; `attribute_uses` is
  `attribution`'s.

Fixtures and tests: `tests/contract/gen_hook_leaf.py` writes
`hook_leaf.jsonl` (not gated, 94 cases, about 44 KB): stdin texts over
Unicode whitespace, non-dict values, invalid JSON, lone surrogates, the
4300-digit bound; payload fields; event windows with mixed kinds, falsy
fallbacks, non-`str` ids and sessions, unhashable sessions, the window's
edges, malformed and offset timestamps and the year-9000 rounding; and
`_emit_hook_attributions` with a fake store, a recording recorder and a
scripted join (joins asked or not, empty server sessions, missing and
failing memories, a failing recorder). Bodies and replies are ASCII, so
no answer reads a Unicode table that differs between releases. Rust:
`golden_hook_leaf.rs`, `hook_leaf_kills.rs` and
`hook_leaf_robustness.rs` (200,000-deep nesting, a megabyte of
U+3000, a hundred thousand events held to linear growth, the
calendar's ends with `i64` lookbacks against the reference's sets, tuple

Left for later units: everything in the map not marked hook-1a.

stamp's transaction. It is cut in two units.

| Function | Reference lines | Needs from the machine | Status |

| `_MAX_VERIFIED_ENTRIES`, `_MAX_VERIFIED_ITEM_LEN` | 59-60 | nothing | built (h_verify-1) |
| `_refuse_stale_stored_claims` | 63-127 | `realpath`, `isdir`, the working directory; the claim oracle as closures | built (h_verify-1) |
| `_refuse_unverifiable_stored_attestations` | 130-199 | as above; `unverifiable_attestations` as a closure | built (h_verify-1) |
| `_SUGGESTED_PATHS_SHOWN`, `_relative_to_root` | 202, 205-217 | `realpath`, the working directory | built (h_verify-1) |
| `_refuse_evidence_free_stamp` | 220-284 | `_worktree_root_is_live`, `detect_path_drift` as closures; `realpath` | built (h_verify-1) |
| `_record_root` | 287-296 | `Anchoring.for_record` as a closure | built (h_verify-1) |
| `_within`, `_is_callers_tree` | 299-307, 310-320 | `realpath`, the working directory | built (h_verify-1) |

| `_stamp`, `_load_verify_snapshot` and the handler | 323-386, 438-885 | the store, the caller, git | unit h_verify-2 |

### What h_verify-1 reproduces (`handlers::verify`)

- Every effect is an argument. `Machine` carries the file system (the
  `Fs` trait), the flavour and `os.getcwd()` (None where it raises).
  `Path(p).resolve(strict=False)` is `os.path.realpath(p)` on POSIX (the
  `Path` spelling drops only empty and `.` components and a trailing
  separator, which the walk skips too), so both go through
  `fsdata::realpath::realpath`; `os.path.isdir` is a `stat` that is a
  directory, any error being False.
- Text is code points. A path is encoded as `os.fsencode` encodes it; a
  code point it cannot encode (a lone surrogate outside U+DC80 to
  U+DCFF) raises UnicodeEncodeError, a ValueError, at the `lstat` of the
  component that holds it, and the port puts a NUL byte there, which the
  walk raises ValueError for at the same `lstat`. A resolved path is
  decoded with `surrogateescape`.
- Every OSError and ValueError of a resolution is caught by the
  reference's guards, so the port reads both as one outcome
  (`Unresolved::Raised`): the gate passes, or the helper answers its
  fallback.
- A `ClaimAnchor` is read for `root` and `convicting` only
  (`AnchorFacts`), a `PathDriftReport` for its three lists
  (`DriftLists`); `load_claims`, `check_claim`, `Claim.render`,
  `claim_reason_is_indeterminate`, `unverifiable_attestations`,
  `detect_path_drift`, `_worktree_root_is_live` and
  `Anchoring.for_record` are closures. `ReadAt` says whether a closure
  was asked with `anchor=` or with `worktree_root=`.
- `_check_verify_args`' `isinstance` checks become `Arg::WrongType`,
  which the JSON layer fills when the handler is ported (h_verify-2):
  the port sees typed values and cannot reproduce a type check itself.
- `_refuse_unverifiable_stored_attestations` passes the ORIGINAL
  `origin_root` on as `worktree_root` where it resolves to a live
  directory, not the resolved path; the port keeps that.
- `_refuse_evidence_free_stamp` keeps the duplicates of `checked` (a list
  comprehension), counts them, and drops what `missing` or
  `expected_absent` hold through a set, as the reference does.
- `_relative_to_root` is `PurePath.relative_to` over two resolved
  absolute paths: component prefix, `.` for the root itself, the path as
  given otherwise.
- Errors are `Refused::ValueError` with the reference's message. Under
  `Flavour::Windows` `realpath` is not ported, and a gate that must
  resolve a path answers `Refused::NotPorted`, a decline (the crate's
  stated Windows gap, ENG-124); a gate that resolves nothing answers as
  the reference.
- `_NOTE_MAX_LEN` (800) is `handlers/_shared.py`'s; the control-token
  refusals are `control_tokens::refuse_control_tokens` with the
  reference's defaults (`BARE_NAME_REMEDY`, `FIELD_WHY`) and
  `_ATTESTATION_REMEDY` for list entries.
- No regular expression is used here (the control-token reader is its
  own unit's).

### Fixtures and tests

- `tests/contract/gen_handlers_verify.py` writes
  `handlers_verify_args.jsonl` (not gated: every type, cap and

- Rust: `golden_handlers_verify_args.rs`,

## Anchoring and the sparse checkout (`verify_anchoring.py`)

`src/bettermemory/verify_anchoring.py`, read at 9b4a365a, decides whether
a record's cited paths are anchored in the working tree it names. It is
cut into units. Unit verify_anchoring-1a (`verify_anchoring/sparse.rs`)
holds the leaves of the sparse-checkout reading; the rest of that reading
is unit verify_anchoring-1b (`verify_anchoring/skip.rs`). Unit verify_anchoring-2a
(`verify_anchoring/report.rs`, `verify_anchoring/anchor.rs`) holds the
report and the claim anchors; unit verify_anchoring-attest
(`verify_anchoring/attest.rs`) holds the attestation write gate and its
predicates; the drift readers are verify_anchoring-2.

The cut: the whole of 598-890 with its fixture world (a MemFs `Rule`
for discovery, stamps that move during a read) is past one unit's
budget, so 1a takes the pure leaves and 1b the parts that read the disk.

### What 1a reproduces

- `config_switch(text, section, key)` takes code points. The text is
  encoded with `surrogateescape` first (a lone surrogate outside
  U+DC80..U+DCFF raises `UnicodeEncodeError`); a text git refuses answers
  None before the name is built, so a name that is not ASCII raises only
  over a text git reads. The name is `str.lower` of `section.key`
  (`unicode::lower`), which must be ASCII: U+212A lowers to `k` and
  matches, U+0130 raises. The last assignment of that plain name wins; a
  value git dies on (`git_bool` None) answers None, as unset does.
- `index_varint(data, pos)` is git's `decode_varint`: each continuation
  adds one before the shift, and a value past 57 bits before a shift
  declines. The reference also accepts a negative `pos` (Python indexing
  from the end); no caller passes one and the port takes `usize`.
- `parse_skip_index(data, hash_len)` reads versions 2 to 4 as the
  reference does: entries padded to eight bytes in versions 2 and 3, a
  name of 0xFFF or more found by its NUL, version 4's prefix compression
  (its varint read against the whole data, the trailer included, as the
  reference reads it), stage 1 to 3 entries passed over but still the
  previous name for version 4, an unknown second-word bit declined, and
  the extensions walked to decline a `link` (split index). An extension
  walk past the end on a 32-bit target saturates where Python's integer
  would not wrap; both stop the walk.
- `SkipIndex::skips(parts)`: the joined name, every directory prefix with
  a trailing slash, then "some below skipped and none below kept", by
  binary search over the sorted lists. The work per call is quadratic in
  the depth of `parts`, as the reference's join per cut is.

No pattern of `re` is used by 1a.

### Fixtures

`tests/contract/gen_verify_anchoring_sparse.py` writes
`verify_anchoring_sparse.jsonl` (not gated): config texts over every
branch of the switch, the varint over every bound, hand-built indexes
(versions 2, 3 and 4, SHA-1 and SHA-256 lengths given explicitly and
crossed, extended flags, an unknown extended bit, a sparse directory
entry, long names at 4,094, 4,095 and 5,000 bytes, stated lengths that
disagree, strips past the previous name, bad versions and signatures,
counts past the data, extensions with and without `link`), `skips` over
eight small worlds, and three sweep rows: every truncation and every
byte set to 0x00 and 0xFF of a base index, pinned by count and SHA-256.
Rows from indexes a real git wrote (cone, non-cone, split) and rows of
`object_format` are left to 1b with its gated sibling.

`verify_anchoring_sparse_robustness` (no panic at the integer bounds,

### What 1b reproduces

`verify_anchoring/skip.rs`, its line ranges confirmed against the
reference at 65aea201. Every function takes the membership rule's `Rule`
(the file system, its flavour, the working directory and the git facts
`object_format` reads), discovery's `Env` where it locates, and
`os.path.expanduser` as a closure.

- `sparse_enabled(ctx, found)` reads the common directory's `config`,
  then the git directory's `config.worktree`, each as
  `Path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")` reads it: decoded
  with one U+FFFD per maximal invalid subsequence, then universal
  newlines (`\r\n` and a lone `\r` read as `\n`). That translation
  changes answers: `[core]` with `sparseCheckout = false`, a lone CR and
  `sparseCheckout = true` reads True, where the raw text makes git's
  parser die. A file that cannot be read is passed over; a value git dies
  on leaves the previous file's answer.
- `parts_below(ctx, path, root)` compares `Path(realpath(...)).parts`
  of both sides. Under POSIX `normcase` is the name itself, so the
  comparison is of bytes; the Windows flavour declines at `realpath`
  (`Failure::NotPorted`, ENG-124).
- `skip_index(rule, found, memo)` stamps the index and the config with
  `githead::discovery::stamp`, answers from the memo when both stamps
  match (moving the key to the most recent end), reads the config only
  where its stamp answered, reads the index, stamps again, and parses
  with the hash length `object_format` names. A stamp that moved during
  the read answers what was read and leaves the memo alone. The memo is
  a `SkipMemo` the caller owns: at most `SKIP_MEMO_CAP` (4) index paths,
  least recently used evicted first, keyed by `Path(gitdir) / "index"`
  as `pathlib` spells it. There is no lock and no registration with
  `_caches`: the owner clears it (`SkipMemo::clear`). Any failed stamp
  or read answers None, as the reference's `except (OSError,
  ValueError)` does; a stamp the Windows flavour cannot take declines.
- `absent_by_sparsity(rule, env, expanduser, memo, path)` walks up with
  `os.path.isdir` and `posixpath.split` to the nearest folder, locates
  with `githead::discovery::locate` (walking, not as git), and asks the
  index for the joined components. The Windows flavour declines before
  any read: the reference answers there through `locate`, which this
  build does not resolve on Windows.

No pattern of `re` is used by 1b.

Decisions. `Path.read_bytes` is a loop of `read_once` over one open
file. The memo holds each `SkipIndex` behind an `Arc`, so a hit hands
out the parsed index without a copy, as the reference shares the object.

Fixtures: `generate_skip` in `tests/contract/gen_verify_anchoring_sparse.py`
writes `verify_anchoring_skip.jsonl` (POSIX only: links on disk, paths
spelled by `posixpath.realpath`): `object_format` over ten config texts
with git read as 2.54, and worlds written to a scratch directory, the
switch in `config` and `config.worktree` (last assignment winning, CRLF,
a lone CR, a value git dies on, a text git refuses, a folder in the
file's place), parts below through symbolic links, skip bits, a sparse
directory entry, version 4, SHA-256 formats crossed with index hash
lengths, no index, a declined index, a split index, a folder for an
index, stamps of the index and of the config that move during the read,
the memo's bound and order over six repositories, a linked worktree, `~`
and a relative path. The native test rebuilds each world in a `MemFs`
and moves a file by rewriting it just before its first open once the
probe reads; the reference moves it in a patched `Path.read_bytes`.
Indexes a real git wrote are not pinned: no gate on the git version
exists, and the hand-built indexes of 1a cover the same layouts.

Tests: `golden_verify_anchoring_skip` (POSIX; the gap recorded by
`verify_anchoring_skip_not_posix`), `verify_anchoring_skip_kills`,
`verify_anchoring_skip_robustness` (a path thousands of components deep,
NUL and non-UTF-8 bytes, a config of 100,000 assignments, an index read in
time linear in its entries).

### What 2a reproduces

- `PathDriftReport` is a struct of owned lists in the reference's field
  order. `to_dict` answers its keys in the reference's insertion order as
  (key, `DictField`) pairs: the six buckets always, then `anchor`,
  `unconfirmed` (path and reason pairs) and `present_but_attested_absent`
  only when `anchor` is set, an empty anchor included. Unequal
  `unconfirmed` and `unconfirmed_reasons` under an anchor answer
  `ZipLengthError` where the reference's strict `zip` raises
  `ValueError`; without an anchor they are not read.
- `ClaimAnchor` keeps every field. `translate` and `holds` are shared
  closures (`Rc<dyn Fn>`); `commit_root` takes `holds_commit` as the
  closure used when the anchor has no memo, and `absolute` takes the
  path rules as the trait `AnchorPaths`. An empty origin root is not
  counted (Python truthiness), and an empty cited commit is not None: it
  skips the caller's store and is asked of a stand-in root, as the
  reference asks it.
- `Anchoring` takes the model as the trait `MembershipModel` (exactly the
  calls the reference makes, `checkout`'s `KeyError` as
  `UnknownCheckout`, the attribute `machine` as a call made once per
  view compared), the caller as `Option<CallerView>`, and `holds_commit`,
  `AnchorPaths` and `expanduser` at construction. The calls reach the
  model in the reference's order and number: `for_record` asks the
  anchor, then the recorded checkout, then the caller's root, then the
  stand-in witness; `prime` passes an id given twice twice. The
  translation and held-commit memos live in a shared part the anchors'
  closures hold, so an anchor never holds its `Anchoring` and no
  reference cycle forms. The held memo is a least recently asked map of
  `HELD_COMMIT_MEMO_CAP` (4,096) answers, a hit moved to the end, a False
  answer kept as a True one is.
- No pattern of `re` is used by 2a.

`tests/contract/gen_verify_anchoring_anchor.py` writes

### What the attestation checks reproduce

Unit verify_anchoring-attest (`verify_anchoring/attest.rs`), reference
lines confirmed at 166a59d7.

- `is_absolute_attestation` is `_is_absolute_attestation`: a `/` or `~`
  start, `$HOME/` or `${HOME}/`, or a first code point `str.isalpha`
  accepts (the crate's Unicode table, so a non-ASCII letter is a drive)
  before a colon and either slash. It is the same test as
  `attestation_paths::absolute_spelling`, written again because the
  reference keeps the two apart.
- `join_under` is `_join_under`: None where `_escapes_root` refuses the
  relative part; else `_normalize_candidate` of `str(Path(root) / rel)`,
  which is `os.path.join` under the host's flavour followed by the
  `PurePath` spelling (`pure_text`: two leading slashes stay two, `.`
  segments and a trailing slash go). The Windows spelling goes through
  `config::pure_path`, which takes text, so a lone surrogate under the
  Windows flavour declines (`Raised::NotPorted`).
- `resolves_under` is `_resolves_under` with `os.getcwd()` as an argument:
  `expanduser` (its raise passed up, as the reference passes it), then
  `isabs`, then both sides resolved by `fsdata::realpath` (non-strict, as
  `Path.resolve(strict=False)` is `os.path.realpath`) and compared by
  parts. An unencodable code point or a NUL is the caught ValueError, so
  False. The Windows flavour declines, the crate's stated Windows gap
  (ENG-124), recorded in `verify_anchoring_attest_not_posix`.
  A path inside a link loop is under the loop, as `realpath` answers on
  CPython 3.13 (3.12's `Path.resolve` raises there, so False): pinned in
  `verify_anchoring_attest_kills`, not in the fixture.
- `worktree_root_is_live` is `_worktree_root_is_live`: `os.path.isdir` of
  the expanded root, an OSError or ValueError of `expanduser` False and
  anything else it raises passed up.
- `unverifiable_attestations` and `unverifiable_at` keep the input order
  and the skip rules: the reference-mode strip, the placeholder test
  before the absolute test, a relative entry skipped without a root, a
  None interpretation or join skipped. `worktree_root` is read as
  `str(Path(worktree_root))` under the host's flavour, spelled at the
  first non-empty entry. Under the Windows flavour a lone surrogate passes
  through the spelling as an unused private-use code point and is mapped
  back, so a surrogate root answers as the reference does; only a root that
  holds both stand-in ranges (U+F0000 to U+F07FF and U+100000 to U+1007FF)
  declines (`Raised::NotPorted`). The closures arrive
  in `Reads`; `_absent_by_sparsity` is asked only for a refusing miss, as
  the reference asks it.
- The anchor is the trait `AnchorView`. The reference reads four things of
  a `ClaimAnchor` here, not two: `root`, `convicting`, `declared_root`
  (whether it is None) and `absolute(path)`, so the trait has those four.
  `ClaimAnchor` implements it in the unit that wires the drift readers.
- `normalize_attestations` answers a `BTreeSet`, the empty key dropped.
- No pattern of `re` is used by this unit.

Left for later units: `_relative_attestation_keys` and
`_is_checkable_citation`, and the `AnchorView` implementation for

| `_VERDICT_FRESH`, `_VERDICT_RECOMMENDED`, `_VERDICT_REQUIRED`, `_VERDICT_RAISE_STATUSES` | `verify.py` 1600-1610 | nothing | built |
| `_COMMIT_DRIFT_ESCALATES`, `_commit_leg_escalates` | `verify.py` 1690-1722 | nothing | built |
| `verdict_from_signals`, `compute_staleness_verdict` | `verify.py` 1725-1800 | nothing | built |

No regular expression is involved.

### What each reproduces

- `candidate_link_rows(memories, ids)` returns a `Vec` of (id, (outbound,
  inbound)) in the order the ids first came, as the reference's dict
  comprehension keeps them; a repeated id keeps its first place. An edge
  is (the link type's value, the other id, the note). A link is kept when
  either end is wanted, and an exact (source, type, target, note) repeat
  is dropped, across repeated memories too. Each list is sorted stably by
  (type, id), so ties keep their order in the snapshot whatever the note.
  A self link lands in both lists. A `HashMap` serves only the look-ups;
  output order never comes from it.
- `DriftMemo<K, V>` holds the memo and the timed-out memo behind one
  `Mutex`, each an insertion-ordered map with move-to-end as
  `OrderedDict` is used. `recall(key, now)` answers the memo first (and
  moves the hit to the end), then a timed-out value when `0.0 <= now -
  kept < 60.0` (the entry keeps its place), else removes that timed-out
  entry; NaN and a clock that went back remove it. `remember(resolved,
  timed_out, now)` sets the resolutions in order (a key already held keeps
  its place and takes the new value), keeps each timed-out value with
  `now` and moves it to the end, then evicts the oldest of each table past
  the cap. `clear()` empties both. The key and value types, the one
  instance and its registration with the cache clearing belong to the
  drift pass; `with_cap` stands in for the patched cap the fixtures use.
- `VERDICT_FRESH`, `VERDICT_RECOMMENDED` and `VERDICT_REQUIRED` are
  defined here, the crate's one home for the three strings; the verify
  unit re-exports them. `verdict_from_signals` takes the status as text,
  as the reference does, so a status outside the four answers as the
  reference answers it; `compute_staleness_verdict` passes
  `VerificationStatus.status.name()`. The counts are `i64` and the commit
  count `Option<i64>`.

### Reference findings (reproduced)

1. `_remember_drift` sets a resolution with `OrderedDict.update`, which
   leaves a key already held at its old place: a key resolved again by a
   later search stays the least recently used and is evicted first. The
   port keeps its place.
2. `_recall_drift`'s docstring says a hit becomes the most recently used
   entry, but a timed-out hit does not move: only a memo hit does.
3. A key kept in the memo and later kept as timed out lives in both
   tables; the memo's value is answered for as long as it is held, the
   timed-out one never.

Stated difference: `render_show` compares `updated` with `created`
iteratively. The reference compares two distinct nested lists
recursively and raises `RecursionError` at a depth that follows the
release and the system; the port answers instead. No golden row holds

Reference finding: `_path_states`' `spelled` strips every leading `.`
and `/` character (`lstrip("./")`), so an attested spelling made only of
them (`""`, `"."`, `"/"`, `"../"`) becomes the tail `/` and joins the
first key ending in `/`, and `"../e"` joins any key ending in `/e`
outside the record's root. Reproduction: `verified_paths=[".", ""]`
with `checked=["/"]` shows one key `/` and no `.` entry. The port
reproduces it.

## Limits and key material

JSON is read and written without recursion, as is `repr`, and a value
nested deeper than `json::MAX_DEPTH` (9998 containers) is RecursionError.
That is where the reference stops when called from the top of a fresh
stack: on Python 3.13.13, `json.loads`, `json.dumps` (compact, indented,
`default=str`), `log.canonical_payload` (its outer dict included),
`repr`, and the head file, origin file and rekey payload reads under
`verify_chain` all take 9998 and raise RecursionError at 9999 (CPython's C
recursion budget, not `sys.getrecursionlimit()`). `repr` counts every
object it spells, a scalar at the bottom too, so it writes 9997 lists
around an int. `review.canonical_json` first walks nested dicts in Python
(`review._thawed`), so a chain of 1000 dicts is RecursionError there from
any caller (`sys.getrecursionlimit()`); native refuses 1000 and takes 999.
`json_edges.jsonl` pins each site's deepest depth and the next one. The
one difference left: the reference's limit is that budget less whatever
its caller's stack already used, so it can stop lower when called deep in
a stack, while the native limit is fixed. Native never rejects what the
reference accepts.

`sort_keys` sorts as Python compares keys: exactly between an int and a
float at any size, and, for fewer than 64 keys, as CPython 3.13's
`list.sort` leaves a NaN key, which compares false both ways (its run
detection changed in 3.13; `json_edges.jsonl`). Past 63 keys with a NaN
among them the order is a fixed total order, not pinned to CPython's.

Seqs are i64, as SQLite stores them; `verify_chain` counts the expected seq
in i128, so a chain that runs to `i64::MAX` reports as the reference does,
and `next_row` after `i64::MAX` is OverflowError (where SQLite refuses the
reference's insert). `log_keyring.jsonl` pins the first against reports
the reference gave, with the head and origin files, the key ring and the
rekey payloads `verify_chain` reads; `tests/robustness.rs` pins the
second, and feeds every public entry point malformed text, JSON,
numbers, head and origin files and rows under debug assertions.

`log::Key` holds key bytes. Its `Debug` prints the length and a
fingerprint prefix, never the bytes, so `KeyRing`'s derived `Debug` is safe,
and no error type carries key bytes. The bytes sit in a `Zeroizing` buffer,
wiped on drop. The store unit, when it reads key files, must keep their
bytes in such a zeroize-on-drop wrapper from the read on (`Key::new` takes
the `Vec` without copying it), not in a plain `Vec<u8>` or `String`.

**What each reproduces.** `KeyFiles::new` refuses an id that is not a
`str` of 32 lowercase hex digits with the reference's ValueError text,
`str(id)[:40]` shown by `repr` (`STORE_ID_PATTERN.fullmatch`, matched by
hand: a class repeated a fixed count, no choice; the pattern is in the
engine's inventory already, which the `ast` scan of `gen_pyre_atom`
finds). The keys directory is parsed as `Path()` parses it.
`load_current` reads the key into a `Key` (zeroized on drop); only
not-found is a missing key, unless the key file or the keys directory
is a link to nothing, which is `KeyUnreadable` with the module's own
reason; any other read error is `KeyUnreadable` with `strerror`'s text,
and the message ends `; the store is not rekeyed over it`.
`retire_current` removes the current key when the retired name is taken
(by anything `Path.exists` sees, 3.13's: ENOENT, ENOTDIR, EBADF and ELOOP
read as absent, any other error raises) and renames it there otherwise.
`write_origin` holds the anchor's lock, writes nothing over an anchor
that parses, and after a file that does not parse reads it again, so an
unreadable anchor raises and stays. `name_origin_key` writes the key's
name only on an anchor at the same seq and MAC that names none (an
ill-shaped name reads as none). `replace_origin` installs or removes the
anchor and returns the one it replaced. `read_binding` raises an OSError
other than not-found and RecursionError, and reads anything else that is
not a non-empty absolute string `path` without NUL as no binding; of two
`path` keys the last wins, as `json.loads` keeps it. `rebind_store`
resolves the store file (3.13's non-strict `realpath`, the working
directory an argument), reads the binding with every OSError as none,
and writes it only when it names another file.

**Decisions.** Files are written by `store::write::replace_retrying`, whose
`replace_atomic` (`store/open.rs`) creates its temporary file 0600 with
`create_new` before the rename; `write_private` then sets the file 0600,
so the umask cannot narrow it, as `mode_before_rename=0o600` does; the
POSIX fixture pins every written file's mode, the lock files' too.
`retire_current`'s rename is `rename_retrying` in `ring.rs`: on Windows a
PermissionError is tried again, five attempts in all from 10 ms doubling,
which is `_fsutil.replace_atomic`'s `_REPLACE_ATTEMPTS = 5` (the store's
`replace_retrying` makes seven). The keys directory's locks go through
the `RingLock` trait; its default, `FileLock`, is `store::write`'s
`open_lock` (created 0600 or opened, kept, `File::lock`), which is
`flock_excl`'s POSIX branch. On Windows the reference locks byte 0 with
`msvcrt.locking` and `File::lock` the whole file, the gap `open_lock` has
today; no test claims Windows lock interop. A follow-up after fsutil2
folds moves `RingLock`'s default and `open_lock` onto
`fsutil::flock_excl`.

`store/open.rs` keeps private copies of `load_current`, `read_binding`,
`same_file`, `is_link_loop` and `binding_text` until a later store unit
moves it onto `log::ring`; the copies in `ring.rs` are deliberate, and
`binding_text`'s Windows prefix stripping is kept in `ring.rs`'s Windows
`resolve`. Until then `open.rs`'s `KeyUnreadable` text lacks the tail
`; the store is not rekeyed over it`, its `read_binding` takes the first
of two `path` keys where the reference takes the last, and it reads a
binding nested past the JSON limit as none where the reference raises
RecursionError.

**Stated differences.** A binding whose `path` holds a lone surrogate
reads as none (the reference returns that `Path`); a store path or link
target that is not UTF-8 is refused or shown lossily. On Windows,
`rebind_store` resolves as non-strict `ntpath.realpath` does, with
`fs::canonicalize` over the longest head that is there (a link inside
the missing tail is not followed), and compares the two spellings
lowered with Rust's `to_lowercase` where `WindowsPath` uses `str.lower`;
the Windows `strerror` is the C runtime's, not asked here. `retire_current`
reads a missing retired name as `Path.exists` does under 3.13, the
pinned interpreter: an OSError other than not-found raises, where 3.14
reads any OSError as absent. No fixture row holds any of these.

**Fixtures.** `gen_log_keyfiles.py` writes `log_keyfiles.jsonl` (the id
check over 21 ids, no file system), `log_keyfiles_posix.jsonl` (POSIX
only: 88 scenarios over a scratch keys directory with links, mode-000
files and folders where files are expected; each the answer or the error

on the Python release: the 6 scenarios whose file is nested 100,000

`log_keyfiles_darwin.jsonl` (platform gated: the message of each
